title: Trump says Putin wants the war to end. Reuters says Putin is preparing to escalate. The diesel shortage across 90% of Russian regions tells you which one to believe.
narrative:
July 9, 2026 — Ukrainian long-range drones struck 35 vessels — primarily shadow fleet oil tankers — in the Sea of Azov over 96 hours, July 6-9, according to Robert "Madyar" Brovdi, commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces. The strikes targeted tankers transporting fuel from Taganrog to Crimea, part of Kyiv's declared "logistics lockdown" of the peninsula. The same 96-hour window: Russia banned diesel exports until the end of July, and Governor Yuri Slyusar of Rostov confirmed two tankers burning in Taganrog Bay.

The political contradiction is between two simultaneous narratives. US President Donald Trump, meeting Zelenskyy at the NATO summit in Ankara on July 8, called Ukraine's fuel infrastructure campaign "an escalation, but it's also an escalation that can help lead to an end" — a public endorsement. Separately, Reuters reported that three sources close to the Kremlin — including one who meets Putin regularly — said Putin had "dug in his heels" to achieve the capture of the remainder of Donetsk, rejected adviser proposals for a ceasefire along current front lines, and was "likely to escalate" in the coming months. Trump also said on July 6 that Putin "wanted the war to end" and a resolution was "closer than people realize."

Putin's public "ready for peace" statements, made during calls with Trump and in press availability, coincide with the week Ukraine's strikes have been most effective against Russia's fuel logistics — suggesting the public posture is a diplomatic counterweight to military losses rather than a genuine signal.
analysis:
The physical evidence contradicts the Kremlin's implied "we're fine" position and the Trump administration's framing that escalation leads to peace.

**Diesel rationing across 90% of Russian regions.** The Ukrainian strikes on refineries and the shadow fleet have produced a documented domestic fuel crisis. Russia banned diesel exports until the end of July — a policy that only makes sense if domestic supply is under genuine pressure. Governor Yuri Slyusar of Rostov confirmed two tankers burning in Taganrog Bay on July 8-9. Crimea-specific fuel shortages prompted Putin to call for direct subsidies to Crimean citizens — an admission that the peninsula's logistics are broken.

**Brovdi's 35 vessels: the named-tanker record.** Brovdi's confirmed strike list includes Chelsea-6, Sanar-1, Sanar-17, Klimena, Penelope, Alexey Savrasov, Venera-3, and Auratanker Sonar-1 — all under Russian flag or sanctioned third-party flags. Russia's Black Sea Fleet has been unable to provide convoy cover. The pro-Russian Telegram channel "Military Informant" explicitly described the tankers as a "shooting gallery" with no air cover from a Black Sea Fleet that "barely defends itself."

**Putin's public vs. private position.** The Reuters sourcing — one source who "meets Putin regularly," two Kremlin-adjacent sources — describes a private posture of defiance and territorial ambition (capturing all of Donbas, creating a "security buffer" beyond current lines) that is structurally incompatible with Trump's public claim that Putin wants to end the war. The timing is notable: Putin's public "ready for peace" statements coincide with the week Ukraine's strikes have been most effective.

**Kostiantynivka claim vs. battlefield reality.** Putin told Trump on July 4 that Russian forces had seized Kostiantynivka. Ukraine denied this. As of July 9, Ukrainian forces were still defending the town, with 29 Russian assault operations recorded in the area in a single 24-hour period — inconsistent with a town already captured. ISW's assessment as of July 9 measured Russian advances at approximately 97 km², not the 3,000 km² claimed by the Kremlin.

**Reuters sourcing: the three-channel credibility test.** The Reuters story's three sources — one who meets Putin regularly, two Kremlin-adjacent — give the report a sourcing depth that the typical Kremlin-denied-X story lacks. The specificity of the "rejected ceasefire proposals" detail and the "likely to escalate" framing about Baltic or Romanian territory is consistent with the pattern of Kremlin signal-testing that preceded previous escalations.
verdict: Trump publicly endorsed Ukraine's fuel infrastructure campaign ("can help lead to the end") while simultaneously telling reporters Putin "wanted the war to end." Reuters sourcing suggests Trump's public characterization of Putin's intent is the opposite of what US intelligence reflects. Putin's private posture — confirmed by three separate Kremlin-adjacent sources — is that he is preparing to escalate, has rejected any ceasefire along current lines, and may be preparing to test NATO Article 5 with isolated strikes on Baltic or Romanian territory. The diesel rationing inside Russia is the most direct physical evidence that the fuel war is working — and that Putin's public escalation of peace signals is a response to that effectiveness, not a sign of strength. The Brovdi 35-vessel strike list with named tankers and the Slusar burning-tanker confirmation are the load-bearing facts; the Reuters sourcing is the credibility layer.
